thread:
nina: Quick sync — customer pilot for surge-credit+priority-lane. We need alignment on launch criteria and contract limits. TL;DR: pilot with 3 customers, 30-day trial, hard cap + overage policy.

raj: sounds good. question: are we coupling priority-lane to a committed spend or letting pay-as-you-go customers opt in?

priya: sales wants a low-friction opt-in for mid-market accounts (< $10k/mo) — they convert faster if they can try without a long commit. Enterprise will get commit discounts.

elaine: finance flag — opt-in without commit means potential spike exposure. need either per-customer softcap or automated throttles to protect SRE costs.

tom: support note — if we expose a burstable softcap, we must ship clear UX and an alerting path. Customers will DM support at the first throttle.

raj: implementation note — two options: 1) softcap + notifications (allow bursts, bill overage) or 2) enforced hard cap with grace buffer. softcap needs meter + queued billing reconciliation. harder to implement cleanly.

nina: proposal: pilot uses softcap with a 2x grace buffer + daily cap notifications. For production GA, move enterprise to hard cap/higher committed tier. Need safety valves for host accounts.

priya: agree on pilot. ask: can we expose a per-route boolean so teams can opt which endpoints use priority-lane? helps customers limit cost to a specific feature.

raj: yes, route-level flag is cheap. bigger cost is routing priority on our infra path and accounting for token-level billing.

elaine: needed launch metrics: conversion rate from pilot to paid, avg overage per customer, p95 cost delta, # of throttle incidents. We need those to model margin.

nina: agreed. add launch criteria: (a) <3 throttle incidents across pilot week per customer, (b) conversion >= 25% within 30 days, (c) median latency improvement >= 30% for priority requests.

tom: ops checklist: 1) customer-facing doc w/ examples 2) in-console toggle + limits UI 3) support playbook w/ escalation path 4) billing statement language.

raj: dev tasks: - API: /projects/:id/priority-lane (POST/GET) - router: weight-based scheduling for priority queues - billing: per-token label `priority=true` - telemetry: tag traces + cost attribution

nina: MVP timeline: two-week dev sprint, then 2-week pilot with first customers. Can we make it non-blocking for other launches?

raj: we can scope router change to an opt-in path so default behavior unchanged. billing changes need a migration script for historical invoices.

elaine: migration risk: ensure we don't double-bill. schedule a dry-run billing report before pilot bill cycle.

priya: customer ask: discount on overage if they commit to 3-month pilot. sales can negotiate but want guardrails.

nina: decision: allow a one-time pilot discount (up to 20%) but require opt-in to billing preview and cap alerts. Also require a PO for enterprise pilots.

raj: blockers: need a short RFC for router weight impl + billing label schema. I'll draft and ping infra.

nina: action items: @raj draft RFC by EOD Friday, @elaine prepare billing dry-run checklist, @priya confirm 3 pilot customers by Monday, @tom draft support playbook.

billing-bot: Reminder — new billing labels must be registered in the schema repo: `priority_lane` (boolean), `surge_credit_id` (string). Please file PR. :robot_face:

nina: thanks all. we'll reconvene next Tue 10am to review RFC + pilot onboarding checklist. :thumbsup:
